_source: Drafted 17 Oct 2026, draft for red-line; see docs/strength-methodology.md. Builds on blueprints/strength.md (signed off 10 Jun 2026). Muscle names follow ExRx anatomical naming; all text original.

patterns.hinge: Bend at the hips with a flat back; hamstrings and glutes do the work.
patterns.single_leg: Split-stance or step pattern, one leg working at a time.
patterns.bridge: Hip extension from the floor or a bench; glute-led.
patterns.hip_stability: Side-hip and inner-thigh strength that keeps the pelvis and knee in line.
patterns.balance: Standing on one leg and controlling the ankle and hip.
patterns.plyometric: Quick jumps and hops: power, tendon stiffness and bone loading.
patterns.carry: Walking with heavy weights: grip and whole-body bracing.
patterns.anti_extension: Core that resists the low back arching.
patterns.mobility: Range-of-movement drills for warm-ups and mobility sessions.

equipment_ids.bench: Flat bench (a sturdy step or box can stand in for some uses)
equipment_ids.db_kb: Dumbbells or kettlebells (either works unless the exercise says otherwise)
equipment_ids.band: Long resistance band or tube; can be anchored in a door
equipment_ids.mini_band: Small loop band (a long band knotted into a loop works)
equipment_ids.mat: Floor space and a mat or towel
equipment_ids.step: A step, stair or low box
equipment_ids.chair: Sturdy chair, sofa or bench to rest a foot, knee or back on

A.name: Full gym
A.note: Matches blueprints/strength.md tier A (back squat / leg press, barbell RDL, barbell hip thrust). Leg press is a fine back-squat swap but is not in this first 40.

B.name: Dumbbells or kettlebells (hotel / home)
B.note: Matches the blueprint tier B mapping (goblet squat, single-leg DB RDL, DB split squat, KB swing). Dumbbell romanian_deadlift and bulgarian_split_squat are the upgrades when the dumbbells are heavy enough. A bench is not assumed: bench press becomes a floor press.

C.name: Bodyweight + band (default, always possible)
C.note: Matches the blueprint tier C mapping (rear-foot-elevated split squat, single-leg RDL reach, step-ups, banded hip thrust). Reps shift up to 8-12 where load can't reach RPE 8. No band? Drop the band exercises and use the band-free swaps in each module.

back_squat.name: Back squat
back_squat.why: Heavy two-leg strength that makes every pedal stroke and running stride cost less energy.

dose.note: Lower under control, stand up fast. Stop about 2 reps short of failure. Do the paired upper-body lift in the rest.

cues: Brace your stomach before each rep
Sit down between your heels, knees over toes
Drive the floor away and stand up fast
mistakes: Knees caving in on the way up
Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom

cautions.knee: Squat only as deep as is pain-free. Still sore? Use a goblet squat to a box or a split squat.
cautions.low_back: Swap to goblet squat or Bulgarian split squat, so the load is held in front or in the hands, not on the spine.
cautions.hip: A pinch at the front of the hip at the bottom means stop above it. Widen the stance a little and turn the toes out.

goblet_squat.name: Goblet squat
goblet_squat.why: The friendliest loaded squat: builds leg strength and teaches a good squat at the same time.

dose.note: When the heaviest weight you have feels easy for 10, move to Bulgarian split squats (or back squats in a gym).

cues: Hold the weight at your chest, elbows pointing down
Sit between your knees with your chest tall
Push up through the whole foot
mistakes: Weight drifting away from the chest

cautions.knee: Squat to a box or chair set at a pain-free depth.
cautions.hip: Stop above any pinch at the front of the hip; a slightly wider stance often helps.

bodyweight_squat.name: Bodyweight squat
bodyweight_squat.why: Grooves the squat pattern and warms up hips, knees and ankles.

dose.note: Mainly a warm-up or first-weeks exercise. Too light as a main lift for most athletes: use a split squat instead.

cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes turned out a little
Sit back and down as if to a chair
Stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top

cautions.knee: Squat to a chair or box at a pain-free height.

bulgarian_split_squat.name: Bulgarian split squat
bulgarian_split_squat.why: Single-leg strength that matches running and pedalling, with enough load to work even at home.

dose.note: Reps are per side. At home with no weights, do 8-12 slow reps. With dumbbells, 6-8. Rest after both legs.

cues: Rear foot laces-down on the bench, front foot well forward
Drop the back knee straight down
Push through the front heel to stand
mistakes: Front foot too close, so the knee shoots forward and the heel lifts

cautions.knee: Shorten the range (stop above parallel) or use a split squat with the back foot on the floor.
cautions.ankle: Hold a wall or doorframe with one hand if balance is shaky.
cautions.hip: If the front of the back hip pulls hard, lower the rear foot (a step, not a bench) or use split squats.

split_squat.name: Split squat
split_squat.why: A stable first step into single-leg strength: both feet stay on the floor.

dose.note: Reps are per side. Hold dumbbells when 12 feels easy.

cues: Take a long stance with the back heel up
Lower the back knee towards the floor
Stay upright and drive up through the front foot
mistakes: Feet in one line like a tightrope, so you wobble
Leaning forward over the front knee

cautions.knee: Stop the back knee a few inches higher. A shorter range is fine.

step_up.name: Step-up
step_up.why: Builds the climbing strength runners and walkers use, one leg at a time.

dose.note: Reps are per side. Box height: top of the box at or just below knee height. Step down slowly: the way down counts.

cues: Put your whole foot on the box
Stand up with the top leg, don't bounce off the bottom one
Step down slowly

cautions.ankle: Hold a rail if balance is shaky.

reverse_lunge.name: Reverse lunge
reverse_lunge.why: Single-leg strength with balance and control, and kinder to knees than a forward lunge.

dose.note: Reps are per side. Alternate legs, or do all reps on one side first.

cues: Step back long and land on the ball of the back foot
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees
Drive through the front foot to step back up
mistakes: Short step, so the front knee takes all the strain

cautions.knee: Shorten the range or go back to split squats.
cautions.hip: Take a shorter step back and keep the body upright.

romanian_deadlift.name: Romanian deadlift
romanian_deadlift.why: Strong hamstrings and glutes: the engine behind climbing and a powerful stride.

dose.note: Barbell in a gym, dumbbells elsewhere. Grip is often the limit, which is fine: it trains grip too.

cues: Soften the knees and push your hips back
Keep the weight close to your legs and your back flat
Stand up by squeezing your glutes
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach lower
Bending the knees so it becomes a squat

cautions.low_back: Only go as low as your back stays flat. Still sore? Swap to hip thrust or single-leg glute bridge.

single_leg_rdl.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
single_leg_rdl.why: Hip strength and balance on one leg: trains the standing leg the way running does.

dose.note: Reps are per side. At home, reach your hands to the floor. Add a dumbbell in the opposite hand when it gets easy.

cues: Tip forward as the free leg goes back, like a see-saw
Keep your hips square to the floor
Push the standing foot down and stand tall
mistakes: Hip opening so the back leg turns out
Bending the standing knee into a squat

cautions.ankle: Touch a wall with one hand until your balance is solid.
cautions.low_back: Keep the range short and the back flat.
cautions.hip: Keep the range short; stop where the standing hip feels pinched or the hamstring pulls sharply.

kettlebell_swing.name: Kettlebell swing
kettlebell_swing.why: Fast, powerful hip drive with no impact: power and back-of-leg stamina in one.

dose.note: This is power, not cardio: end the set as soon as the bell slows. A dumbbell held by one end works.

cues: Hike the bell back between your thighs
Snap your hips forward to float it to chest height
Let it drop and hinge again; the arms only guide
mistakes: Squatting the swing instead of hinging
Lifting with the arms or leaning back at the top

cautions.low_back: Skip during a back flare-up. Use glute bridge or hip thrust instead.

hip_thrust.name: Hip thrust
hip_thrust.why: Builds the glutes that drive hip extension on the bike and in every running stride.

dose.note: Gym: barbell over the hips with a pad. Home: a band across the hips held down by your hands, or a dumbbell on the hips. Pause 1 s at the top.

cues: Upper back on the bench edge, feet flat, shins upright at the top
Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down
Drive the hips up until knees, hips and shoulders are in a line
mistakes: Arching the low back at the top instead of finishing with the glutes
Feet too far away, so the hamstrings take over

cautions.low_back: Stop at a flat body line. Don't over-arch.
cautions.knee: Move your feet a little further out if the front of the knee aches.

glute_bridge.name: Glute bridge
glute_bridge.why: Wakes up and strengthens the glutes with no load on the spine: a safe first step.

dose.note: Good in warm-ups and for beginners. A band above the knees, pushed apart, works the side glutes too.

cues: Lie on your back with heels close to your bottom
Press through your heels and lift your hips
Squeeze your glutes hard for a second at the top

single_leg_glute_bridge.name: Single-leg glute bridge
single_leg_glute_bridge.why: One-leg glute strength that keeps your pelvis level when you run.

dose.note: Reps are per side. Put your shoulders up on a sofa to make it harder.

cues: One foot down, the other knee pulled in or leg held straight
Drive through the heel to lift your hips
Keep both hips level

cautions.low_back: Hug the other knee to your chest to stop the back arching.

banded_lateral_walk.name: Banded lateral walk
banded_lateral_walk.why: Strengthens the side-hip muscles that stop your knee caving in when you land.

dose.note: Band above the knees is easier; around the ankles or feet is harder. Works well in the warm-up.

cues: Sit into a half-squat, chest up
Step sideways and keep the band tight
Don't let your feet snap together
mistakes: Standing up tall and swaying the body

cautions.knee: Put the band above the knees, not below.
cautions.hip: Use a lighter band and smaller steps.

copenhagen_plank.name: Copenhagen plank
copenhagen_plank.why: Strong inner thighs and side trunk: protects the groin and steadies the pelvis.

dose.note: Per side. Start short lever: knee on the bench. Go long lever (ankle on the bench) when 30 s is easy.

cues: Lie on your side, top knee (or ankle) on the bench
Lift your hips until your body is straight
Bring the bottom leg up to meet the bench, then lower slowly
mistakes: Jumping straight to the long lever

cautions.knee: Use the knee-on-bench version: it takes strain off the inside of the knee.
cautions.shoulder: Work from the forearm with the elbow under the shoulder.
cautions.hip: Groin pain during it means stop: use side plank instead until it settles.

calf_raise.name: Single-leg calf raise (straight knee)
calf_raise.why: Strong, springy calves and Achilles: your main shock absorbers when you run.

dose.note: Per side, off a step. Beginners start on two feet. Eccentric option: rise on two feet, lower on one over 3 s. Add a dumbbell when 15 is easy. Aim for about 25 clean single-leg reps before hopping work.

cues: Ball of the foot on the step edge, knee straight
Rise as high as you can
Lower slowly until the heel drops below the step
mistakes: Rolling out onto the little toes

cautions.ankle: Hold a wall. If the Achilles is sore, work on flat ground and keep pain at 3/10 or less.

bent_knee_calf_raise.name: Bent-knee calf raise (soleus)
bent_knee_calf_raise.why: Trains the soleus, the deep calf muscle that takes a big share of the load on every running stride.

dose.note: Per side. Keep the knee bent about 30-45 degrees the whole time. Gym: seated calf machine. Home: a dumbbell on the knee or a loaded backpack.

cues: Bend the knee and keep it bent
Rise onto the ball of the foot
Lower slowly to a full stretch
mistakes: Straightening the knee as you rise

cautions.ankle: Hold a wall. Stay on flat ground if the Achilles is irritable.

single_leg_balance.name: Single-leg balance (reach / perturbation)
single_leg_balance.why: Retrains the ankle's reflexes: proven to cut repeat ankle sprains, and balance work cuts falls later in life.

dose.note: Per side. Progress in order: eyes closed, then reach the free foot to 3 points, then react to a gentle push or catch a ball, then stand on a cushion.

cues: Stand tall on one foot with a soft knee
Keep the arch of the foot lifted and toes relaxed
Reach or react, then come back to still
mistakes: Gripping the floor with the toes

cautions.ankle: Start next to a wall. Master a firm floor before using a cushion.

banded_ankle_eversion.name: Banded ankle eversion
banded_ankle_eversion.why: Strengthens the muscles on the outside of the ankle that resist rolling it.

dose.note: Per side. Sit with the band round the forefoot, anchored on the inside. Hold the end position for 1 s.

cues: Keep the heel still and the knee pointing up
Turn the sole of the foot outward against the band
Return slowly
mistakes: Turning the whole leg instead of the ankle

pogo_hops.name: Pogo hops
pogo_hops.why: Short, stiff bounces that make the Achilles springier and load your bones in a safe dose.

dose.note: Quality over quantity: quiet, quick contacts. Start with 2 x 10 on two feet. Add sets before height. Only after 4 weeks of pain-free calf raises.

cues: Stay tall with knees almost straight
Bounce off the balls of your feet, heels just kiss the floor
Spend as little time on the ground as you can
mistakes: Bending the knees so it turns into a squat jump

cautions.ankle: Firm, flat floor only. Wait until you can balance 30 s on one leg without a wobble.

squat_jump.name: Squat jump
squat_jump.why: Turns strength into power and loads bone with a short, safe impact.

dose.note: Every rep at full effort, with full rest. Land softly into a quarter squat and stick it before the next jump.

cues: Dip quickly into a quarter squat
Jump as high as you can, arms swinging up
Land softly on the balls of your feet, knees over toes

cautions.knee: If landing hurts, swap to kettlebell swings or extra hip thrusts.
cautions.hip: Skip if landing hurts the hip; use hip thrusts instead.
cautions.ankle: Swap to low two-foot pogo hops.

push_up.name: Push-up
push_up.why: Upper-body pushing strength for life, with a plank built in.

dose.note: Hands on a bench or wall makes it easier; feet up makes it harder. Stop 2-3 reps before form breaks.

cues: Hands just wider than your shoulders
Body straight from head to heels
Lower your chest to the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees

cautions.shoulder: Keep elbows tucked and shorten the range. Hands on a raised surface reduces the load.
cautions.low_back: Squeeze your glutes so the hips don't sag.

dumbbell_bench_press.name: Dumbbell bench press
dumbbell_bench_press.why: Builds chest and arm strength, with each side doing its own work.

dose.note: Bench if there is one. No bench? Do it lying on the floor (floor press). Upper-body work stays at RPE 7-8: it supports the legs, it doesn't take over.

cues: Feet flat, shoulder blades squeezed back
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest
Press up and slightly in
mistakes: Bouncing the weights off the chest

cautions.shoulder: Use a palms-facing grip and stop a little short of the bottom.

overhead_press.name: Standing dumbbell overhead press
overhead_press.why: Strong shoulders and a stable trunk for anything you lift overhead.

dose.note: Standing makes the trunk work too. One arm at a time is fine.

cues: Squeeze your glutes and keep your ribs down
Press up and slightly back so the weights finish over your ears
Lower to shoulder height under control
mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears

cautions.shoulder: Skip if pressing overhead hurts and do push-ups instead. Swimmers in a big swim week drop to 2 sets.
cautions.low_back: Don't arch to finish the rep. Kneeling on one knee helps.

bent_over_row.name: Bent-over dumbbell row
bent_over_row.why: Upper-back strength for good posture on the bike and a strong pull in the water.

dose.note: Hinge to about 45 degrees and hold it: your hamstrings and back work too. Beginners: one hand on a bench, one arm at a time.

cues: Hinge forward with a flat back
Pull the dumbbells to your lower ribs
Squeeze the shoulder blades together, then lower slowly
mistakes: Yanking with the arms and shrugging

cautions.low_back: Rest one hand on a bench and row one arm at a time.

lat_pulldown.name: Lat pulldown
lat_pulldown.why: Builds the lats, your main swimming muscle, and a strong back.

dose.note: Pull to the upper chest, never behind the neck.

cues: Grip just wider than your shoulders, lean back slightly
Pull your elbows down to your sides
Let the bar rise slowly to a full stretch
mistakes: Swinging the body to move the weight

cautions.shoulder: Use a palms-facing handle and skip the very top of the stretch if it pinches.

pull_up.name: Pull-up
pull_up.why: The best bodyweight pull: lats, arms and grip all at once.

dose.note: Can't do one yet? Jump to the top and lower slowly over 3-5 s, or loop a band under your feet. A doorway bar at home counts.

cues: Hang with straight arms and shoulders pulled down
Drive elbows to your ribs until your chin clears the bar
Lower all the way under control
mistakes: Half reps that never reach straight arms

cautions.shoulder: Use a palms-facing grip, or swap to lat pulldown.

straight_arm_pulldown.name: Straight-arm pulldown
straight_arm_pulldown.why: Copies the swim pull: trains the lats to sweep the arm from overhead to the hip.

dose.note: Band anchored high (top of a door) or a cable in the gym. Arms long with a slight elbow bend.

cues: Hinge slightly, arms long and up in front holding the band
Sweep your hands down to your thighs with straight arms
Squeeze the lats for a second, return slowly
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a triceps pushdown

cautions.shoulder: Start from below shoulder height if reaching up pinches.

band_pull_apart.name: Band pull-apart
band_pull_apart.why: Balances all the forward reaching of swimming and riding: healthier shoulders, taller posture.

dose.note: Great in the warm-up. Palms facing up works more of the rotator cuff.

cues: Arms straight out at shoulder height, band tight
Pull the band to your chest by squeezing your shoulder blades
Return slowly without shrugging

cautions.shoulder: Do it below shoulder height if it pinches.

band_external_rotation.name: Band external rotation
band_external_rotation.why: Strengthens the small rotator cuff muscles that keep a swimmer's shoulder centred.

dose.note: Per side. Elbow tucked at your side with a small towel between arm and body. Light band: this is control, not a strength test.

cues: Elbow at your side, bent to 90 degrees
Turn the hand outward against the band
Hold a second, return slowly
mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body
A band so heavy you twist your trunk

cautions.shoulder: Stay in the pain-free range. This one is usually fine even with a sore shoulder.

farmers_carry.name: Farmer's carry
farmers_carry.why: Grip and whole-body strength. Grip strength tracks closely with long-term health.

dose.note: Heavy enough that you want to put them down by the end. One weight in one hand (suitcase carry) works the side trunk harder.

cues: Stand tall, shoulders back and down
Squeeze the handles hard
Walk with short, steady steps

cautions.low_back: Go lighter and shorter, and stay tall.

dead_bug.name: Dead bug
dead_bug.why: Teaches your trunk to stay still while arms and legs move: the base of a steady stride and stroke.

dose.note: Per side. Breathe out as the arm and leg reach. Slow is the point.

cues: Lie on your back, arms up, knees over hips
Press your low back gently into the floor
Reach the opposite arm and leg out, return, switch
mistakes: Low back lifting off the floor

cautions.low_back: Move only the legs, or reach less far.

front_plank.name: Front plank
front_plank.why: A trunk that holds its shape when you're tired: on the bike, on the run, in the water.

dose.note: Holding past 60 s adds little. Make it harder instead: squeeze everything, or lift one foot.

cues: Elbows under your shoulders
Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down
Breathe steadily

cautions.low_back: Drop to the knees. Stop if your back aches.
cautions.shoulder: Put your hands or elbows on a bench.

side_plank.name: Side plank
side_plank.why: Strengthens the side trunk and hip that stop your pelvis dropping each stride.

dose.note: Per side. Knees bent is easier; lifting the top leg is harder.

cues: Elbow under shoulder, feet stacked
Lift your hips into a straight line
Don't let the hips roll back
mistakes: Shoulder hunched up to the ear

cautions.shoulder: Do it from the knees, or standing with your forearm on a wall.

pallof_press.name: Pallof press
pallof_press.why: Trains your trunk to resist twisting, so power goes into the pedals and the water, not into wobble.

dose.note: Per side. Hold 2 s with the arms out on each rep.

cues: Stand side-on to the anchor, band at your chest
Press your hands straight out and hold 2 s
Don't let the band turn you
mistakes: Standing too close, so there's no tension

bird_dog.name: Bird dog
bird_dog.why: Gentle back and hip control: a core exercise almost any back tolerates.

dose.note: Per side. Hold 3-5 s at full reach.

cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips
Reach the opposite arm and leg out long
Keep your back flat like a tabletop
mistakes: Lifting the leg so high the back arches

cautions.knee: Kneel on a folded mat or towel.

leg_swings.name: Leg swings
leg_swings.why: Loosens the hips before you load them.

dose.note: Per side, forward-back and side-to-side. Hold a wall. Let the swings grow gradually.

cues: Hold a wall and stand tall
Swing forward and back, then across the body and out
Build the range gradually
mistakes: Bending at the waist to fake range
Swinging hard from the first rep

cautions.low_back: Keep the swing small and the trunk still.
cautions.hip: Small, slow swings only; stop short of any pinch.

knee_to_wall.name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobility
knee_to_wall.why: Frees up ankle bend for squats, lunges and running, and doubles as a quick ankle check.

dose.note: Per side. Move the foot back until the knee only just touches. Note that toe-to-wall distance now and then: a clear left-right difference is worth flagging.

cues: Foot a few inches from the wall, heel down
Drive the knee forward to touch the wall, over the 2nd-3rd toe
Hold 2 s, then ease back

cautions.ankle: A pinch at the front of the ankle means stop at that point. Don't force it.

hip_flexor_stretch.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
hip_flexor_stretch.why: Opens the front of the hip that tightens after hours on the bike or at a desk.

dose.note: Per side. Squeeze the glute of the back leg: the stretch comes from tucking the pelvis, not lunging deep.

cues: Half-kneel with the back knee on a pad
Tuck your pelvis and squeeze the back glute
Shift forward a little until you feel the front of the hip
mistakes: Lunging forward without tucking the pelvis

cautions.knee: Put a folded towel under the back knee.
cautions.hip: Gentle only; a pinch at the front of the hip means ease off the tuck.

thoracic_open_book.name: Thoracic open book
thoracic_open_book.why: Restores upper-back rotation for breathing in the swim and a comfortable position on the bike.

dose.note: Per side. Breathe out as you open. Knees stay stacked on the floor.

cues: Lie on your side, knees bent to 90 degrees and stacked
Sweep the top arm over to the other side, eyes following the hand
Keep the knees together on the floor
mistakes: Forcing the arm to the floor

cautions.shoulder: Bend the elbow and keep the hand on your chest.

run.notes: Calves (straight and bent knee) in both sessions: they carry most of the load in running. Single-leg work is the main lift in Session B. Plyometrics from build, after 4 weeks of pain-free calf raises. Heavy squat/hinge stay in Session A.

bike.notes: The heaviest module: heavy two-leg lifts are what improve cycling economy. Impact work is kept for bone, because cycling alone doesn't load bone. Kettlebell swing needs tier B; at tier C use pogo_hops.

swim.notes: Lats, shoulder blades and rotator cuff come first. Lower-body lifts stay for health and bone, since swimming gives bone little stimulus. Count shoulder load: in big swim weeks cut overhead pressing to 2 sets, and never take shoulder work near failure.

triathlon.notes: Bike module sets the main lifts (heavy). Run module sets the sport block. Swim module lives in the warm-up and the upper-body pull slot (pulldown / pull-up / straight-arm pulldown), so it costs no extra time.

health.applies_to: Everyone. Layered on top of the sport module; it is the whole programme for athletes with no sport goal.

requirements.upper_body: At least 1 push and 1 pull in every session.
requirements.bone_heavy: At least 1 lower-body lift a week at 6 reps or fewer and RPE 7+ (level 2 and up).
requirements.bone_impact: At least 1 plyometric a week once cleared (see beginners rule).
requirements.grip: farmers_carry, pull_up, romanian_deadlift or kettlebell_swing every week. Tier C has no carry: use pull_up if a bar exists, else accept the gap.

health.notes: Health needs every major muscle group, heavy loading and impact for bone, balance and grip. For no-sport athletes the sport block becomes this balance-and-grip block. Adults 65+: see the older-adults decision in docs/strength-methodology.md.

issues._note: Each athlete can carry their own issues. This extends profile.injuries[] (existing fields: location, description, protocol, status, source; physio_allowance and ramp_state stay as lib/injury.py uses them). No parallel store. Never put a real athlete's name or details in this file.

location.note: Free text, kept. lib/strength_ask.py asks about it in the debrief; lib/injury_scope.py matches on it.

area.note: Normalised from location. Drives which exercise cautions apply.

status.note: Legacy 'cleared' reads as resolved (lib/session_library.py already treats both as not current).

priority.note: first = the protocol's sessions are placed before any other training that week.

sessions.title: string
sessions.session_type: optional: a session-library type, e.g. ankle_mobility or mobility, for short sessions outside the cap

items.name: free text, only when the exercise is not in the library
items.pattern: optional pattern id, so a free-text item counts toward coverage

protocol.note: A plain string is still valid (legacy). Code that prints the protocol as text (lib/athlete_brief.py) must read protocol.summary when it is an object.

avoid.note: Never prescribed while the issue is not resolved.

plyo_cleared.note: Only the issue's source sets this to true.

physio_allowance.note: Per-sport zone caps for run/bike quality (lib/injury.py). Unchanged.

other.note: No automatic cautions: rely on the avoid list and the source's protocol.

rules.current: An issue is current unless status is resolved (or legacy cleared). Only current issues trigger the rules below.
rules.priority_first: priority first: place the protocol's sessions before anything else that week. Swim, bike and run fit round them, keeping the 8 h gap from quality sessions where possible.
rules.counts_toward_cap: Protocol sessions with counts_as_strength true count toward the weekly strength cap (strength_max). Two such sessions fill the cap.
rules.counts_toward_coverage: Protocol items count toward weekly coverage by their exercise's pattern (or the item's pattern field for free-text items).
rules.top_up_only: The builder only tops up coverage the protocol leaves missing, usually upper body and core as a 10-20 min add-on appended to a protocol session. It never adds a competing lower-body session.
rules.never_edit_source: Never change a physio's or doctor's exercises, sets, reps or loads. The coach may only point out a conflict (e.g. a hard ride the day after a heavy protocol session) and ask the athlete to check with the source.
rules.self_managed: Protocols with source self or coach may be progressed with the library's progression rules.
rules.cautions_auto: For each current issue, every library exercise's cautions[area.caution_key] apply automatically: follow the caution text or swap.
rules.avoid_list: Exercises on avoid are never prescribed while the issue is current.
rules.plyo_block: No plyometric-pattern exercises while any lower-limb issue is active or rehab, unless that issue has plyo_cleared true. Managed issues don't block.
rules.free_text: Protocol items may use name instead of ex for exercises not in the library. They show without an animation and are added to library_candidates.
rules.debrief: The strength debrief asks about the issue area (already in lib/strength_ask.py).
rules.review_by: On or after review_by, ask the athlete for an update and whether the source has changed anything. Never expire an issue silently.
rules.outside_cap: Short sessions with counts_as_strength false (balance, mobility) sit outside the cap and use the session_type given (e.g. ankle_mobility, mobility).
rules.taper_race_week: Follow the source. If it says nothing: keep rehab sessions, drop top-ups. Draft: see docs/strength-methodology.md decision 6.

template.alternation: Session A and Session B alternate across the week (blueprint).

blocks.picks: leg_swings always + 1 lower mobility drill (knee_to_wall or hip_flexor_stretch) + module.warm_up_add + 1-2 lighter ramp-up sets of the first main lift. 3 min easy spin or row first if a machine is there (blueprint).
module.power[A|B] from the module's from_phase. Skipped for level-1 athletes in their first 4 weeks, and blocked by issues.rules.plyo_block. Done fresh, before the main lifts.

Two pairs. Each pair = 1 lower-body lift + 1 upper-body lift, alternated so the upper lift fills the lower lift's rest. Session A: pair 1 squat + pull (vertical first, else horizontal); pair 2 hinge + push_horizontal. Session B: pair 1 single_leg + push (vertical first, else horizontal); pair 2 bridge (or single_leg_rdl) + pull.
module.sport_block[A|B]. Multi-sport athletes use the triathlon module. Skip picks already covered that week by an athlete's issue protocol (issues.rules.top_up_only).

2 rounds. Across the session: 1 anti_extension + 1 anti_rotation + 1 lateral_core. Session B may swap one for farmers_carry (grip + lateral). In base (no power block yet) core can run to 7 min, as in the blueprint.

hinge.note: At least one true hinge (romanian_deadlift, single_leg_rdl or kettlebell_swing) a week from level 2.

bone_impact.note: Once cleared: level 2+, or level 1 after 4 weeks.

bone_heavy.rule: At least 1 lower-body lift a week at 6 reps or fewer, RPE 7+ (level 2+).

template.issue_protocols_first: Before steps 1-4: place the athlete's issue protocol sessions (issues block). They count toward the strength cap and weekly coverage; the builder then only tops up what is missing.

pick_order.rule: The athlete's module sets which patterns fill each slot, the power pick and the sport block. Health is always layered on.
Use this week's tier. If an exercise needs kit the athlete lacks, use exercise.swaps[tier]. If the athlete is on a higher tier and swaps lists an upgrade for it, use the upgrade.
Only exercises at or below the athlete's level. Use easier/harder to move along the ladder.

For each of the athlete's issues that is not resolved: drop exercises on its avoid list, block plyometrics per issues.rules.plyo_block, and apply each exercise's cautions for the issue's area (follow the caution text, or swap to an exercise with no caution for that area).

athlete_levels.1: New to lifting, or under 3 months of steady training.
athlete_levels.2: 3+ months of 2 sessions a week with good technique on level-1 lifts.
athlete_levels.3: A year or more, solid technique on level-2 lifts.

template.one_session_week: If only one session fits (peak, travel, a busy week): run Session A, but swap the squat for the single-leg pick every other week, and keep the sport block.
template.progression_rule: Add load when every set hits the top of the rep range at RPE 7 or less for 2 sessions in a row, then restart at the bottom of the range. No more load to add (tier C, or the heaviest dumbbell)? Add reps, then slow the lowering to 3-4 s, then move to exercise.harder.
template.regression_rule: Drop 5-10% load, or move to exercise.easier, if reps fall below the range or RPE hits 9+ in 2 sessions running, or if pain goes above 3/10 or is still there the next morning.
template.notes: RPE uses the reps-in-reserve scale: RPE 8 = about 2 reps left, RPE 7 = about 3. Never train to failure. Tempo = seconds lowering - pause - lifting; X = as fast as possible. In example sessions, items with the same 'pair' label alternate; rest_s is the rest after each item, so the lower-body lift gets the combined rest. swaps[tier] = the exercise to use on that tier; a missing tier means keep this exercise.

intro.applies_to: Level-1 athletes, or anyone back from a 4+ week break: first 3 weeks.
intro.note: Learn the movements. No power block. Single-leg and upper body use the same dose.

base.progress: Add load weekly when the progression rule is met (blueprint).
base.notes: Blueprint: full template, progress load weekly. Kept. Main lift 3 x 5 @ RPE 8 as signed off; 5-6 gives the progression rule room.

build.progress: Add load weekly when the progression rule is met. Lift with fast intent on the way up.
build.notes: Blueprint: full template, progress load weekly. Kept; power block added.

specific.progress: Hold the load from the end of build. Nothing new.
specific.notes: Blueprint: maintain load, 2 working sets. Kept exactly.

peak.progress: Same load, fewer reps. Nothing new, no soreness.
peak.notes: Blueprint: 1-2/wk, maintenance, nothing new. Kept. NB session-library.json peak menu lacks strength_general (see decisions).

taper.sport_prehab: Sport-block work 1-2 sets. No slow-lowering (eccentric) emphasis anywhere: it causes soreness.
taper.progress: Same load as specific, very few reps: a neuromuscular touch only.
taper.notes: Blueprint: 1/wk light, none in race week, neuromuscular touch only. Kept. NB session-library.json taper menu lacks strength_general (see decisions).

offseason.progress: The best time of year to build strength: progress load weekly, try harder ladder steps.
offseason.notes: New: not in the blueprint. The planner already has an offseason phase. Draft: see docs/strength-methodology.md.
